Newcastle disease virus strain AF2240, a highly pathogenic avian virus, can induce apoptosis at an early phase of its life cycle.

Newcastle disease virus (AF2240) induces apoptosis in human breast carcinoma (MCF-7) cells at an early phase of the virus life-cycle, possibly during virus binding or virus fusion with the cell-membrane.

Newcastle disease virus Malaysian strain induces apoptosis at an earlier stage of virus replication, possibly during the virus binding or fusion process, through the activation of mitochondrial-related pathways, and that this induction of apoptosis is independent of virus replication and protein production.
